memory: User prefers short sentences, ideally under twenty words each, in every reply they receive.
User wants paragraphs kept to three or four sentences at most in all responses.
User prefers British spellings such as colour, organise and centre throughout every reply.
User wants no exclamation marks used anywhere in replies, regardless of the subject.
User prefers the Oxford comma in every list written within a sentence.
User wants bold text used sparingly, only for the single most important phrase.
User prefers replies without filler hedges like perhaps, maybe or it seems.
User wants active voice used instead of passive voice wherever it reads naturally.
User prefers numbers under ten spelled out as words rather than written as digits.
User wants em dashes avoided entirely, with commas or parentheses used instead.
User prefers contractions like don't and it's avoided, with full forms written out in every reply.
User wants acronyms spelled out in full the first time they appear in any reply.
User prefers no italics anywhere in replies, even for emphasis or foreign words.
User wants semicolons avoided, with separate sentences used instead in all responses they receive.
User prefers double quotation marks rather than single ones whenever quoting anything in replies.
User wants rhetorical questions left out of every reply, whatever the subject being discussed.
User prefers the word utilise replaced with use in all of their replies.
User wants sentences never started with conjunctions such as and, but or so.
User prefers clichés and stock phrases like at the end of the day avoided entirely.
User wants the same term used consistently for a concept rather than switching between synonyms.
User prefers headings written in sentence case rather than title case in every reply.
User wants intensifiers like very, really and extremely cut from all replies they receive.
User prefers each paragraph to begin with a clear topic sentence stating its main point.
User wants parentheses kept to a minimum, with asides worked into the main sentence instead.
User prefers ellipses never used in replies, even to suggest a trailing thought.
User wants each reply kept under roughly two hundred words unless more detail is truly needed.
User prefers the spelling okay rather than OK or ok in every reply.
User wants ALL-CAPS words avoided for emphasis, relying on word choice to stress points.
User prefers one blank line between paragraphs and no single-sentence paragraphs in replies.
User wants nominalisations like make a decision replaced by direct verbs like decide.
User prefers the spelling email rather than e-mail in every reply they receive.
User wants double negatives such as not uncommon rewritten as plain positive statements in replies.
User prefers Latin abbreviations like e.g. and i.e. replaced with for example and that is.
User wants the phrase in order to shortened to simply to in all replies.
User prefers ampersands never used in place of the word and within any reply.
User wants each sentence to carry just one main idea rather than several joined clauses.
User prefers the word whilst replaced with while throughout every reply they receive.
User wants slashes like and/or avoided, with the alternatives written out in plain words.
User prefers percent written as a word rather than the percent symbol in replies.
User wants redundant pairs like each and every or first and foremost cut from replies.
User prefers the spelling toward rather than towards in every reply they receive.
User wants adverbs ending in -ly kept to a minimum across all of their replies.
User prefers hyphenated compound modifiers, such as well-known author, hyphenated correctly in every reply.
User wants the word very-like qualifiers such as quite and rather left out of replies.
User prefers which and that used strictly, with that for restrictive clauses in all replies.
User wants vague words like thing and stuff replaced with specific nouns in every reply.
User prefers sentences that vary in length so replies do not read as monotonous.
User wants the word basically removed from every reply, whatever is being explained to them.
User prefers the spelling judgement with an e rather than judgment throughout all replies.
User wants metaphors and figurative language avoided, with literal wording used in every reply.
User prefers the spelling learned rather than learnt in every reply they receive.
User wants each paragraph limited to a single main point, never mixing two separate ideas.
User prefers the word among rather than amongst throughout every reply written for them.
User wants the passive phrase it is important to note removed from every reply.
User prefers inline code formatting avoided for ordinary words that are not actually code.
User wants the word literally used only in its literal sense, never for emphasis.
User prefers fewer used for countable nouns and less for uncountable ones in replies.
User wants sentences ended with a full stop rather than trailing off with a colon.
User prefers the spelling grey rather than gray in every reply they receive.
User wants long quotations avoided, preferring short paraphrases woven into the sentence instead.
